_comment: WHERE A MOTORWAY VIGNETTE IS NEEDED – and which roads it covers. The lookup for the
guarded by `workers/lint/routing.py`, copied whole into the app.
Only what doesn't change per trip: whether the country sells one and where it applies.
Whether the USER has one is app state, mixed in by `profile.py`.
A VIGNETTE ISN'T A TOLL: it's paid for TIME on a network, a toll per PASSAGE (`toll=yes`),
These data change by law, not by OSM, so every entry has a primary `source` and a
`state`: `verified` (compared with the source, dated) or `unverified` (must be checked
before the app trusts it). `required_on` are OSM classes, which the graph knows.

_states.verified: compared with the primary source – `verified_on` says when
_states.unverified: UNVERIFIED. While this stands, it must not reach the app as fact.

SK.name: Slovakia
notes: The vignette covers vehicles up to 3.5 t; above that a distance toll applies, another question.
Some motorway sections are exempt (city bypasses) – that needs `toll=no` on them in OSM;
until then the detour is sometimes needless.

AT.name: Austria
notes: ON TOP of the vignette some sections have a section toll (Brenner, Tauern, Arlberg):
`toll=yes`, handled by `avoid_toll` – the vignette doesn't pay those tunnels.

HU.name: Hungary
notes: Hungary also sells COUNTY vignettes, so "I have one" isn't one answer for the country;
this lookup treats a vignette as national – a county one gets a route that allows too much.

CH.name: Switzerland
notes: No short-term vignette exists – only an annual one.

PL.name: Poland
PL.system: no vignette; toll per passage on some motorways
notes: THIS IS THE THIRD ANSWER, not "I have none": motorways needn't be avoided at all;
tolled sections are `toll=yes` and belong to `avoid_toll`.
